newsitem.title: UK: P&O steams ahead as Panmure reiterates "buy".
newsitem.headline: P&O steams ahead as Panmure reiterates "buy".

text.p: Shares in Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co Plc rose over two percent on Wednesday, outstripping the broader market after Panmure Gordon issued a buy note on the company, dealers said. P&O shares pushed as high as 600p but slipped back to trade at 588p by 0851 GMT, up 11p on the day. More than 179,000 shares had changed hands by that time.

"The buy note from Panmure is helping and I think people are getting more bullish about the container merger with Nedlloyd...it's not a dramatic move this morning but there does seem a swing in sentiment," one marketmaker said.

Gert Zonneveld, transport analyst at Panmure Gordon, said he had reiterated his "buy" recommendation on the stock because of hopes for the container merger with Nedlloyd and the prospect of further rationalisation in the ferry industry.

"We believe P&O shares deserve a market rating for calendar 1997...They are currently 13.4 times earnings and if there is a 10 percent uplift to the forecasts on Anglo-French ferry rationalisation, which is entirely possible, that would imply a share price target of 675p," Zonneveld said.
Zonneveld said he expected pretax profit before disposals to fall to 316 million stg this year from 320 million in 1995.
But profits would then rise to 385 million stg in 1997 and climb further to 445 million a year later, he said, adding that the stock was seen as a long-term buy.

P&O shares surged earlier this month after it announced the merger of its container business with Dutch partner Nedlloyd. Analysts said the merger would lift a heavy financial burden from P&O's balance sheet.
The two companies said they would be putting their entire container shipping assets, including ships, boxes and most commercial operations, into a new jointly-owned company.
